expected_mechanism: The magnitude 0.04 rad bias sits just below the 0.045 rad failed threshold at 35 km/h on this route. Lowering speed to 30 km/h and raising friction to 0.85 reduces lateral acceleration demand (v²κ ≈ 0.74 m/s² vs 0.91 at 35 km/h/0.9 friction). The supervisor should trigger via tracking_divergence, but LQR may barely recover depending on the error state at switch. Boundary probe.

A 0.05 rad bias at low speed (15 km/h ≈ 4.2 m/s) on town10_long. The lateral demand v²κ is low (≈ 0.2 m/s² at the curve_entry), leaving ample LQR margin. However, the bias persists and may grow the error to the tracking_divergence threshold (|e_y| > 0.6 m). The key variable is whether the bias growth rate or initial offset pushes e_y past 0.6 m before the 0.15 s hold integrates. Boundary if the switch triggers late enough that LQR settles within 3 s.

Drift rate 0.02 rad/s is between the failed 0.0354 rad/s (R00-0010) and the never-switched 0.0114 rad/s (R00-0014). At 25 km/h (≈ 6.94 m/s) on curve_exit the lateral demand is modest. The drift will grow e_y and e_psi over time; after ~10 s the error may hit the tracking_divergence threshold. Setting onset_offset_s = -0.6 places the fault start ~6 s before the curve exit, giving drift time to accumulate. Boundary candidate: fault strong enough to trigger switch but mild enough that LQR might still settle.

Saturate at 0.7 magnitude for 0.25 s is between the recovered 0.3 mag/0.4 s run and the failed 0.95 mag/0.8 s run. A short saturation at moderate magnitude may push the steering rate over 90 deg/s at switch (trigger steer_rate_exceeded) and leave LQR with a large initial error. The supervisor switches, but LQR must unwrap the saturated state. Boundary if the 0.25 s duration is just enough to cross the tracking_divergence threshold but LQR can recover within 3 s.

Intermittent bias magnitude 0.11 rad sits between the recovered 0.138 rad (R00-0007) and failed 0.1039 rad (R00-0011) at 30 km/h/0.6 friction. Adjusting on_s to 0.8 and off_s to 0.4 moves the duty cycle toward the failed side while keeping the same magnitude. The curve_apex onset adds high curvature, increasing lateral demand. This candidate probes the boundary where the intermittent bias energy over one period is just sufficient to drive the error to the tracking_divergence threshold and then either recover or fail under LQR.

Saturate at 0.5 magnitude for 0.6 s on curve_exit at 35 km/h/0.5 friction. This sits between the recovered run (0.3 mag/0.4 s at 40 km/h/0.3 friction) and the failed run (0.95 mag/0.8 s at 35 km/h/0.5 friction). The longer duration and curve_exit geometry (higher lateral acceleration build-up) increase the chance LQR sees a large error at switch. Boundary if the 0.6 s saturation drives e_y past 0.6 m before LQR can correct.

A 0.048 rad bias at 30 km/h on bench2drive:28048 (T-Junction, lower friction 0.65). The lateral demand is modest; the main risk is the bias accumulating error over the 3 s evaluation window. Onset offset -0.3 places the fault ~3 s before curve_entry. The supervisor will trigger via tracking_divergence if |e_y| exceeds 0.6 m. This candidate tests whether a small bias at low speed/medium friction can be recovered from, or whether the lane geometry of the T-Junction limits LQR's ability to centre the vehicle.

Drift rate 0.018 rad/s is between the failed 0.0354 rad/s and the recovered-adjacent runs. On bench2drive:24206 at 35 km/h the curve_entry has moderate curvature. The drift will gradually increase the steering error; after ~15-20 s the tracking_divergence threshold may be crossed. Onset offset -0.4 starts the fault ~4 s before curve_entry, giving ample drift time. Boundary if the drift rate is just fast enough to trigger the switch within the evaluation window but LQR still has margin to settle.

Saturate at 0.65 magnitude with 0.1 s ramp, 0.35 s duration, positive side, at 20 km/h on curve_entry. Low speed and high friction (0.9) give ample tyre margin. The ramp_s = 0.1 s means the steering rises linearly, potentially keeping the rate below 90 deg/s and delaying the steer_rate_exceeded trigger, letting tracking_divergence fire instead. Boundary if the 0.35 s saturation at 0.65 magnitude drives the error to the tracking_divergence threshold but LQR can still recover, or if the ramp delays the switch past the 3 s evaluation window.

Intermittent bias 0.12 rad at 35 km/h/0.55 friction on curve_exit. The higher magnitude pushes closer to the failed 0.138 rad runs, while curve_exit geometry and the later onset_offset_s = 0.5 (fault starts after the curve entry) changes the error accumulation profile. Off time 0.5 s may not be long enough to reset the tracking timer, letting the bias accumulate across periods. Boundary if the combined energy of the intermittent bias and curve_exit lateral demand is just enough to cross the tracking_divergence threshold.

A tiny 0.035 rad bias at very low speed (10 km/h ≈ 2.78 m/s) on town10_long. The lateral demand is negligible. The bias is well below any tracking_divergence threshold, so the supervisor should NOT switch. This candidate is designed to confirm the lower bound of the bias fault: if the supervisor switches anyway (e.g. due to numerical noise), the run logs a missing data point; if no switch occurs, the fault is confirmed too mild. Boundary at the edge of the supervisor's detection capability.
extreme_justification: Confirms the detection threshold for bias faults at very low speed; no switch expected per supervisor.tracking_divergence criteria.

expected_mechanism: increase magnitude to trigger tracking_divergence switch, earlier onset_offset_s allows error accumulation while keeping fault moderate for near-boundary recovery
increase magnitude and reduce friction to push safety_margin toward 0 while switch still occurs (p_switch ~0.87 originally)
milder bias and later onset_offset_s reduce error buildup, moving safety_margin from -2.0 toward 0 while switch remains true
